description: MisoStory values for the Beginner skills (Three Snails 0001000, Recovery 0001001, Nimble Feet 0001002) that MeowDB MS Classic does not publish. Every canonical number (SP, max level, MP and shell costs, fixed damage, HP totals, durations, cooldowns, speed bonus, cast positions, the Three Snails search band and its 800 ms action) is read from game/data/canonical/formulas/beginner.json, attack_speed.json, attack_styles.json and movement.json; this file only fills their documented gaps. Read by scripts/core/skills/skill_def.gd (SkillRules). See docs/runtime/COMBAT.md "Beginner skills".

recovery_heal.reason: Canonical: Recovery restores a fixed HP total (24 / 48 / 72) across its 30 s duration (beginner.json skills[0001001] output_note); MeowDB does not say how that total is spread (beginner.json gaps: 'How Recovery distributes its HP total over 30 s (tick interval): not documented'). MisoStory heals in equal ticks every 5 s, the first 5 s after the cast and the last as the effect ends: 6 ticks, so every level heals a whole number per tick (4 / 8 / 12) and exactly the canonical total. If a total does not divide evenly, tick k heals floor(total x k / n) - floor(total x (k - 1) / n), which still sums to the total. The heal runs whatever the player does (the skill 'recovers HP constantly'), but never above Max HP and never while dead.

buff_cast.reason: Recovery and Nimble Feet: MeowDB gives no cast animation time ('Timing unavailable' on both skill pages; beginner.json gaps, attack_speed.json gaps). MisoStory does not invent one: the cast is instant, so it neither plants the player nor blocks the next action. Both skills cast on the ground, in the air or on a rope, as canonical cast_position says. Zero is a choice too, recorded here so it can be replaced when a timing is published.

three_snails.whiff_consumes_costs_reason: MeowDB does not say what a Three Snails cast with no monster in its search band does. MisoStory follows the classic attack-skill behaviour: the cast happens (the shell flies its 300 px range, or until a wall stops it, terrain_check, and hits nothing), and the shell and MP are spent, as a basic attack swings at nothing.
three_snails.terrain_check_reason: Source-data gap: 'Wall and platform interactions are not confirmed for this skill' (beginner.json skills[0001000] terrain_note, attack_styles.json gaps). The owner ruled on 2026-10-06 (#6) that walls block it: the hit is still decided at the moment of the throw, by a line-of-sight test from the player to the target (SkillSight, from the canonical 28 px aim line above the feet to the target's body centre). The target is the nearest monster in the canonical search band that has a clear line, so a nearer monster behind a wall is skipped. Only terrain and buildings block (sight_blocking_hulls); monsters, Wooden Boxes and props do not. If no monster in the band has a clear line, the shell flies straight ahead until it meets a wall or its 300 px range ends, and the shell and the MP are spent (whiff_consumes_costs). The basic attack is unchanged: it tests no walls. The search band itself is canonical (attack_styles.json three_snails_targeting and ranged_search_bands); its depth across the facing is the shared isometric attack depth (misostory/combat.json isometric_reach.attack_box_depth_px), the same isometric adaptation the basic attack uses. The canonical value stays a source-data gap: this rule ends when a source publishes the skill's wall and platform behaviour.
three_snails.sight_blocking_hulls_reason: What counts as terrain and buildings for the line-of-sight test (#6), read from the world's collision (WORLD_RUNTIME.md 'World loading, collision and containment'): the export's Ground and Walls trimeshes (terrain, cliffs, terraces and the maps' own architecture) and the island's scenery chunks always block. Everything else with collision is a prism per placed object, named '<object>_hull<k>' (crates, barrels, fences, lamps, signs, benches, stalls, carts, trees, boulders, hedges, furniture): those are props and do not block, except the objects listed here, matched by the end of the object's name. The list is the project's own asset kit (src/misostory/kit and maps/*.py @asset tags): the Architecture assets tagged house, shed or facade (houses, shops, the Amherst and Southperry buildings and their wall pieces), the towers (lighthouses, the oven tower, the lookout), the portal doors built into mounds and gates (tagged portal_door), and the terrain pieces the export also cuts into prisms (the plinth outcrops and the rock arch of Snail Hunting Ground II). An object added to the kit with one of those tags needs its name added here. Monsters (their own physics layer) and Wooden Boxes (no physics body) are never tested.
three_snails.projectile_reason: Presentation only. The hit is resolved when the shell is thrown (the damage number appears at once, as for a basic attack), because MeowDB publishes no projectile speed and a delayed hit would let the target move or die in flight. The shell model flies from the player to the target at 18 m/s (the 7.5 m reach in about 0.4 s) and is 0.22 m across, read on the gameplay camera.

effects_on_death.reason: MeowDB does not document what happens to an active buff or a skill cooldown when the character dies. MisoStory ends the active skill effects at death (Nimble Feet's speed and the rest of Recovery's heal are lost), as classic MapleStory cleared buffs at death, so a heal-over-time never runs while the death notice is up. Cooldowns keep counting down: dying does not reset them.
